query: For a titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy in a single-phase solid-solution state, whose elevated-temperature mechanical performance remains unestablished when titanium and nickel serve as primary constituents rather than additions, what single testable intervention hypothesis could produce better mechanical properties under elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing than the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, mechanism, predicted relative outcome, applicable composition and test-regime boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials to a titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy in a single-phase solid-solution state will improve its mechanical properties under elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing.
generation.intervention: Addition of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable solid solution phase
generation.mechanism: Sluggish diffusion effect, severe lattice-distortion effect, high-entropy effect, and cocktail effect
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical properties, such as high strength, superior oxidation resistance, tensile strength, and fracture resistance
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties of the alloy without the addition of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials
generation.boundary: Composition and test-regime boundaries, such as the range of oxygen or nitrogen additions (1-3 atomic %) and the operating temperatures of potential applications (e.g., 700° to 800°C)
generation.uncertainty: Long-term stability of the alloy under potential service temperatures, behavior of oxygen/nitrogen interstitials during high-temperature aging

falsification_experiment.design: High-temperature mechanical testing and microstructural analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of oxygen or nitrogen interstitials does not improve the mechanical properties of the alloy under elevated-temperature or extreme-environment testing, the hypothesis is falsified.

Equimolar Ti-V-Nb-Ta has an extremely high compressive yield strength, 1273 MPa at room temperature and 688 MPa at 900°C (). By comparison, conventional high-temperature Ni-base superalloys notably soften above 600°C, with the compressive yield strength dropping to ~200 MPa at 900°C (). Equimolar Ti-V-Nb-Ta also exhibits impressive tensile ductility, ~14% at room temperature (), and a relatively low brittle-to-ductile transition temperature between −47° and −27°C, comparable to BCC metals and stainless steels for engineering applications (, ).
Despite these advances, the bulk of experimental work studying the Ti-V-Nb-Ta system and other RHEAs has focused on materials under the as-cast or homogenized conditions. These conditions may not accurately represent their long-term structural/mechanical stability at service temperatures. As a newly developed material system, a comprehensive understanding of their long-term stability under potential service temperatures remains to be established. ## Abstract
The CoCrFeNi system is one of the most important high entropy alloys (HEAs) systems. By adding and adjusting the alloy element components and using different synthesis methods, different phases, organization and microstructure can be obtained, thus improving their properties. In this study, CoCrFeNiTix HEAs with various Ti contents (x in molar ratio, x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) were fabricated by an electrochemical process by virtue of different oxides. The impacts of different Ti contents on the structure, distribution of elements, mechanical properties and corrosion behavior were researched using XRD, EDX and other testing methods. The bulk CoCrFeNiTix (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5) HEAs could be obtained through vacuum hot pressing sintering process (VHPS), which had a single-phase FCC structure. The results of the study showed that the bulk CoCrFeNiTix exhibited superior ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and hardness, with the UTS of CoCrFeNiTi as high as 783 MPa and the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi1.5 reaching 669 HV.
